cf.title: JIT inlining SIGSEGV in MemoryBuffer::getFile with LLVM 17 / GCC 13

input.subject: [PATCH] JIT inlining SIGSEGV in MemoryBuffer::getFile with LLVM 17 / GCC 13

verdict_reasoning: No objection to the idea or the design survived. The patch moves one call onto the C API that load_module() already uses, in one file. The only surviving objection, maintenance-fit-2, is fixable: message #1 states the std::optional<Align> layout as the cause but does not confirm it. That gap affects the commit message and the back-patch decision, so a committer who knows the JIT code has to judge it.

brief.title: JIT: load inline summary through the LLVM C API to avoid crash
brief.problem: With LLVM 17 and GCC 13 on openSUSE Leap 15.6, JIT inlining crashes the backend with signal 11 inside llvm::MemoryBuffer::getFile(), called from llvm_load_summary(). With jit_above_cost and jit_inline_above_cost set to 0, about a hundred check-world tests fail. It affects builds where Postgres and the distro libLLVM use different compilers.
brief.proposed_design: llvm_load_summary() reads postgres.index.bc with LLVMCreateMemoryBufferWithContentsOfFile() instead of the C++ MemoryBuffer::getFile(), as load_module() already does. The author blames the std::optional<Align> default argument, built at the call site, whose layout a GCC 13 build and a distro libLLVM.so.17 need not share. The change touches only src/backend/jit/llvm/llvmjit_inline.cpp.
author_claims: Skipping llvm_inline() makes check-world pass, and Ubuntu with LLVM 18 does not crash.
A small C++ program calling getFile("/etc/hostname") crashes the same way, while the C API works on the 2.4MB index.
With the patch, the boolean join returns 4 rows and 6 functions are inlined.
The crash is the other face of the ABI problem in BUG #18254, where FreeBSD with LLVM 16 could not resolve the getFile symbol.
The C API is a stable contract between compilers, so the fix belongs in tree and is not a local toolchain problem.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. The author copies Andres and Thomas, but nobody has replied.
unclear: The author shows no evidence that the std::optional layout mismatch is the actual cause, such as a disassembly or a reproduction with matching compilers.
The message does not say which compiler built the openSUSE libLLVM.so.17.
The message does not say whether other C++ LLVM calls in llvmjit, which may share the same ABI risk, were checked.
The message does not say which LLVM versions the patch was tested on beyond 17 and 18, or which branches it should go to.
The message does not say whether error handling on a missing or unreadable summary file stays the same with the C API.
search_queries: LLVM C API instead of C++

objections.title: Root cause unconfirmed, so the change may hide a packaging fault
objections.failure_scenario: The real cause is something else, such as a libstdc++ or header mismatch in the openSUSE packages. The patch hides it at this site. The fault then surfaces at another C++ call, and maintainers debug llvmjit code that has already been patched on a theory nobody confirmed.
objections.argument: Message #1 blames the std::optional<Align> layout but gives no disassembly and no build with matching compilers. It also does not say which compiler built libLLVM.so.17. The standalone C++ program crashing on /etc/hostname points toward a toolchain or packaging defect outside Postgres. That kind of defect may belong with the distro.
objections.author_must_show: Does the crash go away when llvmjit.so is built with the compiler and C++ library that built the openSUSE libLLVM.so.17?

critic.reasoning: The commit message states the std::optional<Align> layout as the cause, but message #1 shows no disassembly, no matching-compiler build, and not which compiler built libLLVM.so.17. The change is safe either way, so the gap affects the recorded rationale and the back-patch decision.

refuted.title: One call site fixed, the rest of llvmjit keeps the same ABI exposure
refuted.failure_scenario: A packager builds llvmjit.so with GCC against a distro libLLVM built differently. Another C++ call with defaulted or by-value standard-library arguments then crashes in the same way, for example during summary parsing or IRMover. Users find out from signal 11 in production with JIT inlining on, and no buildfarm member reproduces it.
refuted.argument: The commit message frames the crash as a general mismatch between a GCC-built llvmjit.so and a distro libLLVM, but it changes only llvm_load_summary(). llvmjit_inline.cpp and the other llvmjit files use the C++ API in many places that have no C API equivalent, such as the summary index and IRMover. Accepting this rationale in tree implies the project supports mismatched-compiler builds, with no test or build-time check to catch the next case. A committer would likely ask whether the project is taking on that support or only fixing this one symptom.
refuted.author_must_show: Were the other C++ LLVM calls in llvmjit checked for the same ABI risk, and is this build configuration one the project should claim to support?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 reports that with the patch getModuleSummaryIndex() works and 6 functions are inlined, so summary parsing and IRMover ran on this toolchain. The patch copies what load_module() already does and adds no support promise; a further crash is a guess.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is a crash fix for LLVM 17 builds, and message #1 does not say which branches should get it.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The change is in llvmjit_inline.cpp, which depends on LLVM interfaces the project does not control.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the crash go away when llvmjit.so is built with the compiler and C++ library that built the openSUSE libLLVM.so.17?
Which compiler and C++ standard library built the openSUSE libLLVM.so.17 package?
Which branches should get the fix, and on which LLVM versions other than 17 and 18 was the patch tested?
Does a missing or unreadable postgres.index.bc produce the same behaviour with the C API as with MemoryBuffer::getFile()?
Were the other C++ LLVM calls in llvmjit checked for by-value or defaulted standard-library arguments?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the LLVM JIT provider and its inlining code. Message #1 copies two people for this area, but nobody has replied.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a back-patched change in the JIT inlining path and for a commit message that records an unconfirmed cause. The code change is one call in one file.
committability.author_follow_up: The author asks for feedback in message #1 and created the CommitFest entry about three weeks later. No later sign.

priority.reason: The crash affects builds where Postgres and the distro libLLVM use different compilers and JIT inlining runs. The patch is 2.7 KB in one file and copies load_module(), but no one has replied since 2026-08-19.

provisional_note: Without the code, the error path for a missing or unreadable summary file and the ownership of the C API memory buffer cannot be checked. The stated cause of the crash is also unverified.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add llvm version into the version string
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the LLVM version to PG_VERSION_STR, the way the gcc version is already shown, so that JIT bug reports include it. A later version takes the runtime version from the loaded library through LLVMGetVersion, an API that exists from LLVM 16 on.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the configure-time llvm-config version may not match the library loaded at run time. He also objected that changing what version() returns can break code that parses it, and that adding subsystem versions to it does not scale to ICU or libxml2. He suggested a new system view instead, the author agreed to try that direction, and others proposed showing both build-time and runtime versions in the view.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Adding rows to a view over time seems way less likely to cause
problems than messing with a string people probably have crufty
parsing code for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enable jitlink as an alternative jit linker of legacy Rtdyld and add riscv jitting support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the LLVM JIT provider use JITLink (ObjectLinkingLayer) in place of RuntimeDyld, through a new C++ wrapper because LLVM has no C API for it. It turns this on for riscv with LLVM 15 or later and hard-codes riscv ABI names, CPU features, PIC relocation and the medium code model.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund said the riscv ABI and target machine settings belong in LLVM, and that the missing JITLink C API should be proposed to LLVM. Thomas Munro asked why JITLink was used only for riscv and why riscv needed manual feature and ABI selection. The author agreed to try the LLVM patches later and asked to keep the workarounds meanwhile. No reviewer replied after that, and no new patch version appears.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this is something that should go into the llvm code, rather than
postgres.

precedents_retrieved.title: JIT compiling expressions/tuple deforming
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds LLVM-based JIT compilation of expression evaluation, tuple deforming and aggregate transition calls, with optional inlining of builtin functions from bitcode. It also includes preparatory executor refactoring and configure support for LLVM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier closed the entry because this thread had stalled, while the author kept working on the patches elsewhere; no objection to the design decided it. The author had also said the series was still far from committable, and he moved the work to a separate commitfest entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I know that you are working on this actively per the set of patches you have sent lately, but this thread has stalled, so I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Lazy JIT IR code generation to increase JIT speed with partitions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch delays JIT IR generation until an expression is first executed, so plan nodes that never run, such as most Parallel Append children over many partitions, are never compiled. A later version also cached the to-be-inlined bitcode modules and cloned them with llvm::CloneModule() instead of reloading them from disk.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that lazy generation emits roughly one module per function, which is inherently more expensive than emitting one module per query. He would not accept a one-function-per-module design as the base for usage-triggered JIT. He also warned that IRMover renames types in cloned modules, which can degrade code quality. David Geier then found that the module cache had stopped inlining altogether, and that cloning early made llvm::CloneModule() so slow that JIT time stayed high, so he stopped work on it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that's just inherently more expensive and thus a no-go.

precedents_retrieved.title: Summary Sort workers Stats in EXPLAIN ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes EXPLAIN ANALYZE so that Sort node statistics from parallel workers are summarized (average and peak sort space used, sort method, number of workers) instead of being printed per worker. This follows the approach already used by show_incremental_sort_group_info() and is meant to reduce output size when many workers are used.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After a review pointing out issues (summary only in non-VERBOSE mode, reporting workers planned rather than launched, unclear text format), the author posted a revised patch, but the patch later failed regression tests on all platforms. A reviewer asked for an updated patch, none was posted, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback for lack of an update.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This has been marked as RwF based on the lack of an update.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_buffercache: Add per-relation summary stats
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a function to pg_buffercache, first pg_buffercache_relation_stats() and later renamed pg_buffercache_relations(), that scans shared buffers once. It returns per-relfilenode and per-fork counts of buffers, dirty buffers, pinned buffers and average usage count, aggregated in a hash table so a query does not need a tuplestore row for every buffer.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Ashutosh Bapat did not want more hand-aggregation functions: they copy what hash aggregates already do and add maintenance cost, for example for testing resizable shared buffers. Reviewers also noted that the in-function hash table does not respect work_mem or spill to disk. The author stopped posting new versions until the work_mem problem was solved, citing unclear interest. The thread then moved to a separate pg_buffercache_pages() tuplestore patch, which was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'll hold off on posting a new version for now, since I think we'd have to figure out a solution to the work_mem question at the very least, and it sounds like right now its also a toss-up in terms of overall interest to get this committed.

precedents_retrieved.title: jit_warn_above_fraction parameter
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, jit_warn_above_fraction, that logs a warning when JIT takes more than the given fraction of a query's run time. The aim is to find queries where bad estimates make JIT cost most of the runtime, so users can tune JIT for those queries instead of turning it off globally.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane doubted that the warning would give useful information, and some earlier objections to the GUC, not shown here, made the same point. He also noted that a message at WARNING level is logged without the statement that triggered it, so it should be at LOG level, which would also change the GUC name. Julien Rouhaud agreed it should be LOG. The patch then stopped applying, a rebase was requested in September 2022, and no new version appears in the visible messages before it was returned in October.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The arguments against the GUC were not about whether it's convenient. They were about whether the information it gives you is actually going to be of any use.

precedents_retrieved.title: JIT compilation per plan node
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the JIT compilation decision from the whole query to each plan node, so a node is compiled when its cost times its estimated number of calls exceeds jit_above_cost. Inlining and optimization stay decided per query, and the patch passes estimated calls through createplan.c with a new CreatePlanContext.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No visible message states why the entry was withdrawn. Tomas Vondra and Robert Haas supported moving the decision to the node level. In the last messages, David Rowley questioned plan node total cost as the measure, proposed using the estimated number of executions of each ExprState instead, and said the costing design was still undecided. The thread then stops, three months before the withdrawal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Anyway, I don't think it's worth talking in detail about specifics about implementation for the total cost of the node idea when the whole replacement costing model design is still undecided.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
We have collected several instances of a workaround for GCC bug 53119,
which caused false-positive compiler warnings.  This bug has long been
fixed, but was still seen on the buildfarm, most recently on lapwing

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P2] covers JITLink and riscv target settings and added a C++ wrapper where LLVM has no C API; this patch moves one call onto an existing C API, so the reason recorded for [P2] does not apply. Message #1 points to BUG #18254, a link failure on the same getFile symbol, but describes it as a bug report, not a rejected fix.

The patch adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour or dump content, and it touches one internal file only. Query results and settings stay the same for existing users, so this angle finds nothing to object to. Whether a missing or unreadable summary file is handled the same way with the C API cannot be checked without the code.

The patch changes only how llvmjit_inline.cpp reads postgres.index.bc into memory. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog change, protocol message or Postgres struct or hook. Nothing persistent or cross-node is involved, and the change does not block backpatching for ABI reasons.

The patch changes how llvm_load_summary() reads postgres.index.bc, a file installed by Postgres itself, and adds no user-visible surface, privilege or setting. Nothing in it changes who can trigger JIT or what a non-superuser can see, so this angle has no objection; the error path on an unreadable summary file can only be checked in the code.
The change itself copies the existing practice in load_module() and touches one file, which lowers confidence in rejection. Both objections concern the rationale and its scope, not the change itself.

Building Postgres with the compiler that built libLLVM, or setting jit_inline_above_cost = -1, avoids the crash, but the second gives up inlining and the first is not how distributions package Postgres. The patch reuses the C API call that load_module() already uses, so it adds no new mechanism, and P2's reason (the work belongs in LLVM) does not apply to a caller-side ABI mismatch.

The demand angle finds no objection. The proposal fixes a backend crash: about a hundred check-world failures on default openSUSE Leap 15.6 devel packages, with an outside report of the same getFile() crash (message #1). The change touches one file and follows the C API call that load_module() already uses, so non-users pay almost nothing. The design and root-cause questions belong to other angles.
